kept.q: Simplify sqrt(50) to its simplest surd form.
kept.explanation: 50 = 25 x 2, and 25 is a perfect square. So sqrt(50) = sqrt(25) x sqrt(2) = 5sqrt(2).
kept.pidgin: 50 = 25 x 2, and 25 na perfect square. So sqrt(50) = sqrt(25) x sqrt(2) = 5sqrt(2).

kept.q: Simplify sqrt(18) + sqrt(8), leaving your answer in simplest surd form.
kept.explanation: sqrt(18) = sqrt(9x2) = 3sqrt(2) and sqrt(8) = sqrt(4x2) = 2sqrt(2). Adding like surds: 3sqrt(2) + 2sqrt(2) = 5sqrt(2).
kept.pidgin: sqrt(18) = 3sqrt(2) and sqrt(8) = 2sqrt(2) because 9 and 4 na perfect squares. Add the two surds wey be same type: 3sqrt(2) + 2sqrt(2) = 5sqrt(2).

kept.q: Chidinma was asked to rationalize the denominator of 3/sqrt(5). What is the correct result?
kept.explanation: Multiply numerator and denominator by sqrt(5): (3 x sqrt(5))/(sqrt(5) x sqrt(5)) = 3sqrt(5)/5. This removes the surd from the denominator.
kept.pidgin: Multiply top and bottom by sqrt(5): (3 x sqrt(5))/(sqrt(5) x sqrt(5)) = 3sqrt(5)/5. Na so you take remove surd from bottom.

kept.q: A student in Kaduna is asked to rationalize 1/(sqrt(7) - sqrt(5)). Which of the following is the simplified result?
kept.explanation: Multiply top and bottom by the conjugate (sqrt(7)+sqrt(5)): denominator becomes (sqrt(7))^2 - (sqrt(5))^2 = 7 - 5 = 2. So the result is (sqrt(7)+sqrt(5))/2.
kept.pidgin: Multiply top and bottom by the conjugate (sqrt(7)+sqrt(5)): bottom go become (sqrt(7))^2 - (sqrt(5))^2 = 7 - 5 = 2. So answer be (sqrt(7)+sqrt(5))/2.

kept.q: If x = 2 + sqrt(3), find the value of x + 1/x.
kept.explanation: 1/x = 1/(2+sqrt(3)). Multiply by the conjugate (2-sqrt(3)) over itself: 1/x = (2-sqrt(3))/(4-3) = 2 - sqrt(3). So x + 1/x = (2+sqrt(3)) + (2-sqrt(3)) = 4.
kept.pidgin: 1/x = 1/(2+sqrt(3)). Multiply with conjugate (2-sqrt(3)) for top and bottom: 1/x = (2-sqrt(3))/(4-3) = 2 - sqrt(3). So x + 1/x = (2+sqrt(3)) + (2-sqrt(3)) = 4, the sqrt(3) go cancel.
